subject.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock

question: Should this PR require side-effect-safe cancellation or late-write guards before merging the auth timeout backstops?
rationale: The patch fixes a real availability failure mode but changes auth-provider and session-state concurrency behavior in a way that green tests cannot prove safe for existing users.

options.title: Require side-effect-safe timeout ownership
options.body: Block merge until timed-out OAuth and runtime auth operations cannot write credentials or active auth state after their lock or single-flight ownership has ended.

options.title: Accept the emergency mitigation risk
options.body: Merge the current deadline-only approach as an availability mitigation while explicitly accepting possible late credential or runtime-auth writes.

options.title: Pause for auth-owner redesign
options.body: Hold the branch until an auth owner provides a concrete design and redacted live proof for the recovery path.

recommendation.title: Require side-effect-safe timeout ownership
recommendation.body: Block merge until timed-out OAuth and runtime auth operations cannot write credentials or active auth state after their lock or single-flight ownership has ended.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history on both the OAuth lifecycle and embedded runtime auth surfaces changed by this PR.
